findings.title: Official notification accounts differ in flight identity as well as stated times
findings.observation: The reproduced September18,2001 NORAD release and FAA table give AA77 notification09:24 and UA93N/A or NA. May23,2003 testimony gives UA93 possible-hijack notice09:16. conflicting_or_qualifying_records: Preserve all versions. The shift09:16 to10:07 is51 minutes of stated anchors, not a calibrated operational delay or measured clock offset. A missing-aircraft notice, hijack notice and inferred flight identity are different events.

The 2001 NORAD release also gives UA17508:43 and estimated crashes09:37/10:03 for AA77/UA93; the FAA table gives UA17509:05 and09:38/10:04 crashes. These facsimile values are retained without normalization.

No independent reconstruction of native radar, phone recordings, log entries or clocks was performed. The Commission’s correction claim is itself preserved as a source position, not selected as controlling by this audit.
findings.next_test: Obtain original NEADS logs/tapes and FAA notice chains with channel provenance and at least two independent clock anchors; retain event types and version dates.

findings.title: DOT reports executives knew a liaison answer was inaccurate and did not correct it
findings.claim_type: Affirmative oversight finding of knowledge plus noncorrection
findings.observation: The QFR claimed the Air Force liaison immediately joined the bridge after08:46. OIG says she joined only after09:37, that three executives learned the answer was inaccurate, and none corrected it with the Commission.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: OIG distinguishes the executives’ later knowledge from their initial reliance on an erroneous chronology. Their reported assumptions about who would correct the answer conflict with the liaison’s account that no one asked her to do so.

FAA’s over6,000 documents/materials supplied to the Commission are stated as mitigation/context, not a reason to erase the knowledge/noncorrection finding.

findings.title: Mineta and the Commission preserve incompatible early/later PEOC timing accounts
findings.observation: Mineta says he reached PEOC about09:20 and heard the exchange about five or six minutes later. The Commission describes Cheney’s conference-room arrival shortly before10:00, perhaps09:58, and different later inbound-aircraft exchanges at10:10–10:18.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: About09:20 versus perhaps09:58 gives a nominal38-minute contrast; conditional09:25–09:26 versus10:10–10:18 allows a44–53-minute forward shift for interval overlap. These calculations do not measure clock error or establish that the two sources describe the same exchange.
The Commission acknowledges conflicting arrival evidence and no documentary evidence for an earlier claimed authorization call, while noting incomplete relevant sources.
Tunnel entry, shelter conference-room arrival and later order exchanges are distinct event types. No original PEOC logs, witness clock calibration or common-event join was authenticated.
findings.next_test: Acquire PEOC Shelter/Watch/Communications/9-11 logs, White House switchboard records, witness notes and calibration evidence; test multiple-event as well as memory/clock alternatives.
